svg.text: Heat: what a tree can do, and what my model cannot see
The evidence behind f1, and the honest boundary around it
WHAT A TREE ACTUALLY DOES
Shade, through mean radiant temperature
MRT is the term a crown changes most; the sun–shade UTCI gap on hot
afternoons is 2.3–4.7 °C in full shade — a lower bound for a real crown
(scripts/heat_bounds.py).
Leaf area sets how much sun gets through
τ = exp(−k · LAI) with k = 0.5 (Beer–Lambert, as in Peng et al. 2026) — k is
an ASSUMPTION: leaf-angle differences alone moved MRT by up to 9.5 °C (Li
2023). Same geometry, different species, different shade.
Transpiration cools the air more — but needs water
1.15 °C against 0.43 °C for shade (Park 2026). In Porta it counts for less,
on two separate Rahman et al. (2019) findings: per leaf area transpiration
is lowest in Mediterranean climates, and it is ~10x lower for trees in paved
pits than over grass.
A heatwave can take the leaf area away
Platanus lost roughly 30–50% of its plant area index after a > 41 °C
heatwave (Sanusi & Livesley 2020) → a low-LAI plane variant in the
sensitivity runs.
WHAT THE MODEL CANNOT SEE (AND HOW I ANSWER IT)
Ladybug ignores evapotranspiration
so it likely underestimates vegetation cooling by about 2–3 °C UTCI
(Mannucci et al. 2025). In a paved Mediterranean street that error is
smaller than elsewhere, which is why I accept it.
Model error 1–2 °C
so I compare the ranking of layouts, not absolute degrees. The optimiser
only ever needs the ranking.
"Share of points above 32 °C" saturates
on the hottest El Prat day even full shade is ≥ 32 °C in 5 of 6 afternoon
hours (2 of 6 on the hot-week day, 3 of 6 on the design day). So the
metric is the mean UTCI over 12–17 h on a design cooling day — decided 19
Oct — with the hottest real day as a check.
Night is outside the design hour
dense clusters trap heat at night (Zölch et al. 2019). Stated as a limit,
not modelled.
So the heat objective is a ranking of layouts on a design afternoon — not a temperature forecast.
A fast shade x transmissivity proxy scores every layout; Ladybug Tier 1 (point UTCI on a 2 m grid) and Honeybee Tier 2 check the shortlist. Infrared City would replace Tier 1 if access is granted.

Sources: notes/methodology.md sections 3 and 6; notes/decisions/heat_objective.md; notes/method_heat_validation.md; Peng et al. 2026, Park 2026, Rahman et al. 2019, Mannucci et al. 2025, Sanusi & Livesley 2020,
Zölch et al. 2019, Bröde et al. 2012 (matrix ids in notes/lit/literature_matrix.csv).
